newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's Emaar details IPO share allotment.
newsitem.headline: UAE's Emaar details IPO share allotment.

text.p: Newly formed Emaar Properties said it had allocated shares to 180,468 applicants in its five-times oversubscribed initial public offering in the United Arab Emirates.

In a statement, Emaar said 183,685 applications worth 3.377 billion dirhams were received for the 657 million dirhams worth of shares offered to the public. It said the mailing of share allotment letters and refund cheques began on May 13.
The issue had been marred by controversy when Emaar announced that it had uncovered widespread proxy share buying.
Locally defined as share buying in the name of other UAE nationals by using their identity cards, proxy purchases are used to overcome low share allotment in IPOs.

"In the final analysis, it was revealed that a little over 160 people had logged in 42.7 percent of the applications...If a linear allotment procedure was adopted, the 160 investors would be cornering shares worth over 285 million dirhams -- leaving just 370 million dirhams for over 100,000 genuine investors," it said.
These 78,497 proxy buyers were allotted only two percent of the shares which they had applied for.
Over 100,000 "genuine investors" had been issued at least the minimum of 500 shares.
Two thirds of Emaar's capital is open to the public. The rest is held by the founders, including the Dubai government with a 10 percent stake.
